raw:
{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence", "note": "Admitting struggle feels like proof they cannot handle the role they have worked hard to earn." },
  "read": "Saying 'I'm fine' is a status-protection move. They have built an identity around being your reliable, high-output person, and acknowledging overload feels like it will cost them that standing in your eyes and their own. The harder they push, the more they are signaling that mattering to you and to the team depends on never showing limits.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Quietly pull work off their plate without telling them, to spare the awkward conversation — but that confirms their fear that showing strain means losing trust and getting sidelined." },
  "mentorMove": "Keep the standard — the work still needs to get done at quality — but open a door that lets them voice what is real without losing face. You are not asking them to admit weakness; you are treating sustainable output as a professional skill you expect them to develop.",
  "holdFirm": ["The quality and reliability of their work is not negotiable.", "Long-term capacity is part of the job, not a personal favor — burning out helps no one on this team."],
  "stayFlexible": ["How the workload gets redistributed or sequenced is fully open.", "Whether this conversation happens one-on-one, over coffee, or as a brief check-in is their call."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, do you have ten minutes? I want to check in, not about a deliverable — just about how things are sitting with you right now." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I have been watching your output and honestly it is impressive. I also know the volume has been unusually heavy the last few weeks. I am not assuming anything is wrong — I am genuinely asking: what does your bandwidth actually look like right now, on a real level?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I care about: I need you performing at your best three months from now, not just this week. If the load is stacked in a way that is chipping away at that, I want to problem-solve it with you — adjust timelines, shift something to someone else, build in a buffer. What would help most from where you sit?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to your best work because I have high standards and I genuinely believe you can sustain them — but sustaining them means treating your own capacity as something worth protecting. Let's agree on one concrete adjustment this week, even a small one, and revisit in two weeks to see if it is working." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Over time, normalize workload conversations as a sign of professional maturity, not a red flag — every time they flag a pressure point early and you respond by problem-solving rather than pulling back their responsibility, you build the kind of trust that makes them a stronger long-term contributor."
}
situation: One of my best people is clearly overworked and heading for burnout but insists they are fine.
